entities.name: Adalram
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalram (died 836) was Archbishop of Salzburg from 821 to 836, serving at a critical moment in the Christianisation of the Danube frontier and the conversion of Moravia — the Slavic kingdom that would later become the stage for the famous Cyrillo-Methodian mission. His archiepiscopate made significant contributions to the missionary expansion of the Frankish Church into the Slavic east.

Salzburg's missionaries had been active among the Bavarian Slavs since the late eighth century, and Adalram continued this tradition. He baptised Mojmir I, the first historically documented ruler of Great Moravia, around 831 — an event of considerable significance for Central European Christian history. Mojmir I's baptism began the Christianisation of Moravia that would be intensified and complicated by the subsequent Cyrillo-Methodian mission (863) and the controversies over Slavic liturgy.

Adalram's archiepiscopate also engaged the continuing development of Salzburg as an ecclesiastical and cultural centre under the Carolingian empire. His contribution to Carolingian Christianity extended beyond the missionary frontier to include the institutional development of one of the empire's most important metropolitan sees.
